This draft is based only on your account: Phase 2 was due 14 days ago, you have received neither delivery nor a response, and you describe Section 11.2 as requiring a written notice that specifies the failure, then 30 days to cure, before default or delay damages. I do not have the signed agreement.

Do not declare default in this notice. The clock you described starts on a specified failure, not on a default finding.

---

**[Date]**

**By [method required by the notice clause]**

**To:** [Nexagrid legal name and notice address in the agreement]  
**From:** [Your legal name and notice address]  
**Re:** Notice of failure to deliver — [Agreement title and date], Phase 2 — Section 11.2

This notice is given under Section 11.2 of the [full agreement title] dated [date] (the “Agreement”).

Under [delivery / SOW / schedule clause and exhibit], Phase 2 [use the Agreement’s name for the deliverable] was due on [contractual due date].

As of the date of this notice, we have not received that Phase 2 delivery. We have also received no communication from you about the missed date.

You are required to cure this failure within thirty (30) days of [receipt / delivery — use the word Section 11.2 or the notice clause uses].

If the failure is not cured within that period, we reserve all rights under the Agreement, including the right to treat the failure as a default and to assess delay damages, in each case only as the Agreement provides. Nothing in this notice waives any right, remedy, or time period.

[Name, title]  
[Company]  
[Contact details required by the notice clause]

---

**Check before sending.** Confirm against the signed text: the exact Phase 2 obligation and due date; Section 11.2’s wording (what must be specified, when the 30 days start, what “cure” means); the notice clause (address, method, copies, when notice is deemed given). A notice that misstates the failure, cites the wrong clause, or is sent the wrong way may not start the cure period.

If today’s date is 11 September 2026, “fourteen days ago” is 28 August 2026. Use the contractual due date, not that informal count.

**Next step:** Insert the Agreement’s names, dates, clause numbers, and notice mechanics, then send only by the method the notice clause requires.
